records.text: Ben Shapiro tried to take over Breitbart, and Steve Bannon ran him out.
records.speaker: Steve Bannon

appearances.snippet: He tried to take over Breitbart and I ran him out of there.

verification.notes: Bannon made the allegation as a former Breitbart executive, but takeover intent and the claim that he ran Shapiro out are not independently established by the available public record.

records.text: Ben Shapiro has attempted hostile takeovers of several companies, including Candace Owens's company.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And yeah, he's tried to take over a lot of companies hostilely, including mine before it even got started.

verification.notes: The alleged hostile takeovers and pre-launch attempt involving Owens's company concern private negotiations and intent unsupported by independently available records.

records.text: Andrew Breitbart hired 28-year-old Ben Shapiro as Breitbart editor-at-large two weeks before Breitbart died.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: But just two weeks before he died, Andrew (Andrew Breitbart) hired a then 28-year-old Ben Shapiro to be the editor-at-large of Breitbart.

verification.notes: Shapiro's contemporaneous resignation statement and later interview confirm he joined Breitbart News as editor-at-large two weeks before Andrew Breitbart's death; Shapiro was 28.

sources.title: Shapiro Resigns From Breitbart News
sources.relevance: Publishes Shapiro's contemporaneous statement that he joined Breitbart News two weeks before Andrew Breitbart died.

sources.title: Ben Shapiro — FRONTLINE interview
sources.relevance: Shapiro recounts joining Breitbart in February 2012 and his history with Andrew Breitbart.

records.text: An internal battle over Breitbart News's direction followed Andrew Breitbart's death.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: There was an internal war that waged about what the direction of this healthy conservative company would be.

verification.notes: Contemporaneous reporting and Shapiro's later account document a sustained internal conflict over Breitbart News's direction and Steve Bannon's leadership after Andrew Breitbart died.

sources.title: Breitbart exodus highlights schism over Trump within conservative media
sources.relevance: Contemporaneous reporting documents the internal split over Breitbart's direction and Bannon's leadership.

sources.title: Ben Shapiro — FRONTLINE interview
sources.relevance: Shapiro describes leadership and editorial conflict at Breitbart after the founder's death.

records.text: A Breitbart executive told Candace Owens and Charlie Kirk that Ben Shapiro started The Daily Wire through a manufactured scandal.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #3 (Ep zSKrxIUMNqw)

appearances.snippet: And a chief shared with us the true story of how Ben (Ben Shapiro) started the Daily Wire on scandal.

verification.notes: The source is an unnamed former Breitbart executive speaking privately; neither the identity nor the manufactured-scandal account can be independently authenticated.

sources.title: Upheaval at Breitbart over dustup with Donald Trump campaign
sources.relevance: Contemporaneous AP/CBS report confirms Shapiro and Fields resigned on March 13, 2016.

records.text: Ben Shapiro accused Steve Bannon of betraying Andrew Breitbart's mission by backing Corey Lewandowski, who Shapiro said allegedly assaulted Michelle Fields, at Fields's expense.
records.speaker: Ben Shapiro

appearances.snippet: Breitbart News under the chairmanship of Steve Bannon has put a stake through the heart of Andrew (Andrew Breitbart)'s legacy. ... In order to protect Trump's bully campaign manager, Corey Lewandowski, who allegedly assaulted Michelle (Michelle Fields).

verification.notes: Shapiro's published resignation statement accused Bannon of betraying Andrew Breitbart's mission and protecting Trump and Lewandowski at Fields's expense.

sources.title: Shapiro Resigns From Breitbart News
sources.relevance: Publishes the quoted accusations against Bannon and Breitbart management.

records.text: The Daily Wire was being built quietly by the end of 2015 but lacked the support its founders expected.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #3 (Ep zSKrxIUMNqw)

appearances.snippet: what really happened was that Ben (Ben Shapiro) had been not happy with the fact that they were not making him the king of Breitbart, had begun quietly building Daily Wire at the end of 2015. Like didn't have enough gumption behind it. People were not getting behind the daily wire in the way that they anticipated they needed a scandal.

verification.notes: The Daily Wire's own history confirms it launched in 2015. The claims that it was built quietly by year-end and lacked the support its founders expected rely on a private account and are not independently established.

sources.title: About — The Daily Wire
sources.relevance: The company's official history confirms a 2015 launch and initial investment, but not the private claim about expected support.

records.text: Ben Shapiro and Jamie Weinstein manufactured the Michelle Fields scandal to give The Daily Wire momentum.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #3 (Ep zSKrxIUMNqw)

appearances.snippet: And they decided to do that. They decided to create a scandal because there was no energy behind it. ... And his best friend Jamie Weinstein decided to cook up a scandal.

verification.notes: Police and prosecutorial review found video evidence that Lewandowski grabbed Fields and probable cause for battery. No reliable evidence supports the claim that Shapiro and Weinstein manufactured the incident to launch The Daily Wire.

sources.title: Florida state attorneys explain why they did not prosecute Corey Lewandowski
sources.relevance: Reports that prosecutors found probable cause and video evidence of the grab, contradicting a manufactured-incident premise.

sources.title: Donald Trump's Campaign Manager Charged for Grabbing Reporter
sources.relevance: Documents the police report, video, and bruising; provides no evidence of a Shapiro-Weinstein fabrication.

records.text: The Fields-Lewandowski scandal permanently damaged Breitbart News.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: By then the damage had been done to Breitbart. They never recovered, by the way. Breitbart never recovered from this scandal

verification.notes: The scandal clearly preceded resignations and internal turmoil, but 'permanently damaged' and 'never recovered' are undefined causal judgments that cannot be verified as stated.

records.text: Candace Owens accused Ben Shapiro of trying to take over Breitbart after Andrew Breitbart died and plotting to take down the company after failing
records.speaker: Candace Owens

And when that failed, he plotted to take down the company because why can't he have it? Doesn't matter if he builds it, it should be his.

verification.notes: The source-scoped transcript context at 00:05:49 records Owens making this accusation. The episode transcript and a contemporaneous report of Bannon's AmericaFest remarks independently establish the conveyance; this result does not treat the underlying takeover allegation as adjudicated fact.
